codex.host: Codex CLI 0.154.0 and the Codex desktop app, Windows
codex.install: local marketplace -> codex plugin add, into the user profile
codex.finding: Plugin hooks work in Codex, but only after the plugin's hooks are trusted. Trust is granted in the desktop app (Hook screen, per plugin and per event); the CLI offers no way to grant it and, until it is granted, runs silently without the hooks.
codex.corrects: An earlier entry in this file claimed plugin hooks were unsupported in Codex. That was wrong. The plugin_hooks feature flag being stage removed does not gate this.
codex.control: The two installs are content-identical -- the hooks key present, commandWindows absent. The earlier one never fired across instrumented turns; this one fires. The only change between them is the user granting trust in the desktop app.

verified_after_trust.control_plain: PASS - ttak, ttak on and ttak off are taken by the UserPromptSubmit hook; the turn completes with 0 input and 0 output tokens
verified_after_trust.state_write: PASS - written to ~/.codex/plugins/data/ttak-ttak-design-local/state.json as {"enabled":true|false}, so the hook does receive the plugin data path
verified_after_trust.injection_on: PASS - the model quoted the core first line, # TTAK
verified_after_trust.injection_off: PASS - asked whether a # TTAK heading is present, the model answered NO

codex.still_broken: The model shell has neither PLUGIN_DATA nor CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA -- confirmed by a direct env probe in Codex, matching Claude Code. The settings skill CLI route fails on both hosts.
codex.ux_note: In codex exec --json a hook-blocked prompt returns a turn with no message and no tokens, so the control succeeds with no visible confirmation. The desktop app shows the hook reason.
not_established: whether trust can be granted without the desktop app
